content.title: Pale Blue Dot: How Small Are We in the Vast Universe?
content.subtitle: The photograph taken on February 14, 1990, that changed humanity's thinking.
content.body:
It was the golden age of ancient Babylon. Standing on his palace balcony, Emperor Nimrod looked across his vast empire. Everything he could see belonged to him. Countless soldiers stood below, and his treasury overflowed with gold. A slight gesture could take someone's life or spare it. The entire kingdom feared him. Seeing his absolute power, Nimrod believed no force could challenge him. In his arrogance, he once told Prophet Ibrahim (AS), “I give life and cause death! I am your lord!”

That Quiet Afternoon in 1990

NASA's spacecraft Voyager 1 was travelling through deep space, nearly 6 billion kilometres from Earth, beyond the Solar System. Renowned astronomer Carl Sagan asked NASA scientists to turn its camera around one last time and photograph our familiar home, Earth.

The camera turned, capturing a historic image. When it reached Earth, scientists around the world stared in amazement. Against the vast darkness of space and a tiny ray of sunlight, our planet appeared as a tiny bluish dot, just 0.12 pixels wide. They named it the 'Pale Blue Dot'.

Our Smallness in the Infinite Universe

According to modern astronomy, Earth is part of the Solar System, located in the Milky Way, a galaxy containing around 100 to 400 billion stars. The observable universe has more than two trillion galaxies like it!

Sunlight takes just eight minutes to reach Earth. Yet light travelling at its own speed would take around 93 billion light-years to cross the observable universe. Before this unimaginable vastness, Earth is less than a grain of sand. And humans, standing barely five to six feet tall on it, are even smaller and more helpless!

The Holy Quran presents this reality clearly. Allah Almighty says:

“Indeed, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know.” (Surah Al-Mu'min: 57)

All Our Pride Trapped Inside a Tiny Speck of Dust!

Close your eyes and imagine: inside the Earth, almost impossible to find with the naked eye on the map of the universe, stood Nimrod's magnificent palace. That almost invisible dot was also home to Pharaoh, Qarun, and countless other arrogant, oppressive, and bloodthirsty rulers. They claimed to be gods and shed the blood of millions for power!

Where is Nimrod now? Where is Pharaoh? Where are their mighty empires? They have vanished into history, buried beneath the earth. Yet, how strange that we still stand on the same tiny speck, suffering from the same disease! A little money in the bank, a position, or a small piece of land can change how we walk. Over petty matters of ego, we cut ties with our brothers, oppress the weak, and imagine ourselves great!

Yet Allah says: “Do not walk upon the earth with arrogance. You can never split the earth apart, nor reach the height of the mountains.” (Surah Bani Isra'il: 37)

So, What Should We Do?

Before the greatness of the Lord who created this infinite universe, trillions of galaxies and countless stars, our existence is less significant than a drop of dew.

Let us stop taking pride in worldly achievements, beauty, wealth or power. Let us bow humbly before the Master of the universe, acknowledge His greatness and majesty, and accept how small we truly are. May our Lord forgive us.

References:

  1. Nimrod and Ibrahim (AS): Al-Quran, Surah Al-Baqarah (Verse 258)

  2. Scientific source: NASA, Voyager 1 “Pale Blue Dot” Image Archive (1990)

  3. The vastness of the heavens and earth: Al-Quran, Surah Al-Mu'min (Verse 57)

  4. The command to avoid arrogance: Al-Quran, Surah Bani Isra'il (Verse 37)

  5. The consequences of even an atom's weight of arrogance: Sahih Muslim (Hadith 91)
